'And I stood up to see till they folded up that old house; and carried off all the pillars, and all the beams and ornaments of the house were at the same time folded up with it, and they carried it off and laid it in a place in the south of the land. candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Animal Apocalypse (1 Enoch 85-90) (c. 150 BC)

'And I saw that a white bull was born, with large horns, and all the beasts of the field and all the birds of the air feared him and made petition to him all the time' — the climactic appearance of the messianic White Bull at the end of the Animal Apocalypse. The white bull echoes Adam (85:3 — Adam was the original white bull); the Messiah is therefore the eschatological New Adam, restoring the original Adamic kingship over creation. All beasts and birds fearing him + making petition to him is the universal recognition of his cosmic authority. The Tewahedo Christological reading takes this as proto-Christological prophecy fulfilled in Christ as the Last Adam (1 Cor 15:45) and the Lamb (Rev) who receives universal worship.

'And I saw till all their generations were transformed, and they all became white bulls; and the first among them became a lamb, and that lamb became a great animal and had great black horns on its head; and the Lord of the sheep rejoiced over it and over all the bulls' — final reunification: ALL become white bulls again (return to the Adamic state). The lamb-with-great-black-horns is the eschatological messianic figure (distinct from the white-bull-with-great-horns at 90:37, which represents the Davidic-messianic line). Tewahedo Christology reads the two figures together: 90:37 (Christ as new Adam — white bull) plus 90:38 (Christ as Lamb-of-God with horns of authority) presents both Christological registers in a single Animal-Apocalypse climax.
